nodes.method: the same 20 seeded catalogue game packets (approve-check --catalogue-sample 20 --seed 20261110) judged on rubric v1 (data/studio-approved/JUDGE-PROMPT.md) by two separate Claude judges given the packets only, one Opus and one Sonnet; pass/fail compared per piece (data/studio-approved/runs/2026-11-10-catalogue-sample/agreement.json)
nodes.title: Sonnet agreed with Opus on pass/fail for 15 of 20 (the bar was 19). It caught both wrong keys, but passed 5 pieces Opus failed: 2 for register, 1 wrong fact, 2 for readability only. So the bulk re-judge is Opus. Tokens for 20 pieces in one agent: Opus 17M cache-read, 0.84M cache-write, 0.10M output; Sonnet 10M, 0.92M, 0.28M.

nodes.method: every catalogue game and explainer rendered in the real Desk tray at p360, p412 and l1366 with its board twin (matrix.mjs, forge3-qa@2; a crashed page retried once), certificatesFromMatrix; table per engine in docs/design/round7/studio/recert-2026-11-10.md
nodes.title: Strict passes at p360/p412/l1366 went from 760/432/690 to 760/409/684, and served from 760/666/690 to 760/671/684. The p360 column is the board twin for every piece, and that twin is the engine's name plus four kit key terms with no figure. On a 360 px phone no child plays a Studio v2 game. At p412, class 4-5 pieces pass the strict 16 px floor 0 of 295 times.

main's ruling: a catalogue piece reaches a child only with a judged pass (rubric v1) in data/studio-approved, exactly like a generated piece; no judged pass means the script's board or the engine's reviewed default. The tray gate reads it (server/forge3/tray-gate.js, cert catalogue-judged), behind the switch STUDIO_CATALOGUE_JUDGED, default on. The bulk judge is Opus (m-r7-catalogue-judge-agreement). Pieces failing on off-topic, wrong key, wrong fact or register are withheld and listed for Learning; readability faults go to the engine.
nodes.reverse: a fresh random sample of 50 unjudged catalogue pieces passes rubric v1 at 95% or better

nodes.title: PROPOSED to main (docs/design/round7/studio/ENGINES-360.md): on a phone, the lesson offers the play family where one covers the topic (186 of 382 catalogue topics, all maths and science). Studio v2 gets a portrait core mode, then portrait layouts only for the engines whose topics no play family covers: story-rail, beat-line and sort-storm (133 of the 196 uncovered topics), then town-lab, era-drop and land-lab. These are language, SST and EVS, where no play family exists, so there the two systems are not substitutes.
nodes.reverse: main decides the twin board at 360 is the phone experience for language, SST and EVS, or the Games stream plans language/SST families
